rounds.text: Victory Electric Vehicles International Ltd trades at a steep discount to its underlying assets, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.69x based on a price of ₹ 13.5 against a book value of ₹ 19.5 [E2]. This valuation discount is further magnified by a price-to-book of 0.72x compared to a sector benchmark of 2.61x [E7]. The market has heavily depressed the stock, leaving it sitting just 2% of the way up its 52-week range [E5]. However, this pessimism ignores the company's historical compounding capacity, demonstrated by a robust median return on equity of 24% over both 3-year and 5-year periods [E18, E19]. On an earnings basis, the stock commands a modest P/E of 15.1 [E1], trading well below the sector benchmark P/E of 23.64x [E6]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], the current ROE has dropped to 7% [E13, E20, E48], and ROA lags the sector benchmark at 4.39% versus 6.25% [E8].

Conceded: the stock trades below its book value at 0.69x [E2] and sits at 2% of its 52-week range [E5], and conceded: the P/E of 15.1 [E1] sits below the sector benchmark of 23.64x [E6]. However, the bull's reliance on historical 3-year and 5-year median ROE figures of 24% [E18, E19] is entirely disconnected from the reality of the business today, where the current ROE has collapsed to 7% [E13, E20, E48]. That depressed current return on equity is not an anomaly, but part of a broader underperformance where the company's ROA of 4.39% actively lags the sector benchmark of 6.25% [E8]. Furthermore, the low valuation multiples and the stock languishing near its 52-week low [E5] are entirely justified by a total lack of shareholder return, evidenced by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Far from being a mispriced compounding machine, the valuation reflects a deteriorating operational reality that makes historical medians irrelevant.
